svg.text: OPERATIONS MANUAL
PART A - GENERAL
9 DANGEROUS GOODS
9.3 CARRIAGE OF WEAPONS
DEFINITIONS
Any weapon that is NOT a weapon of war or ammunition of war may be
classified as a sporting weapon. Sporting weapons include hunting knives,
bows and other similar articles and antique historical weapons that were
once classified as a weapon of war or munitions of war such as muskets.
A firearm is any device that fires a projectile, such as a gun, pistol or rifle.
Guidance for how to determine whether the firearm may be classified as a
sporting weapon is by their typical use:
(a) Shooting animals.
(b) Target shooting such as targets or clay pigeons.
(c) Air guns such as starting guns and starting pistols.
CARRIAGE OF SPORTING WEAPONS
The Operator is approved by the Authority to carry sporting weapons in
accordance with the provision given under 2. All sporting weapons must be
carried in the baggage hold and be inaccessible to the passengers at all
times during flight.
All jet aeroplanes satisfy the requirements for the inaccessible baggage hold.
The B200 series aeroplanes are the ONLY propeller driven aeroplanes having
a suitable inaccessible baggage hold if fitted with the cargo pod.
CARRIAGE OF AMMUNITION
Different types of ammunition may be carried up to a total weight of 5 kg per
passenger. The ammunition must be packaged in accordance with the
technical instructions.
The ammunition must be transported in a baggage area that is inaccessible
to the passengers during the flight.
NOTIFICATION OF THE COMMANDER
The commander must be notified of the presence and location of any
sporting weapons on board, however, there is NO requirement for a written
record.
